📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-ms-account-api-4xx-spike-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #50 (last_notified_at was 2026-08-05T11:32:14Z — ~3d23h14m ago, 24h suppression window had expired).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin`
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: monitor 299551518 in 'No Data' or newly-modified state, but NOT accompanied by a genuine >300/15min 4xx count. 2) Run the evidence_query directly against the actual 4xx-hits metric -- if it's in the single digits (or empty), this is the known noise pattern. 3) Check service:ms-account-api status:error DD Logs -- expect 0 hits, consistent with all prior documented occurrences. 4) If the metric DOES show a genuine breach (hundreds of 4xx in 15 min), treat as a real incident and do not apply this KB entry -- retract the 'noise' diagnosis.
Open Jira: n/a — fix_status monitoring-noise-suspected-unconfirmed

Source alerts (1 total):
  • n/a — degraded cycle, no Slack MCP this session (proxy: DD monitor 299551518, fired 2026-08-09T10:46:19Z)

Root-cause analysis:
  • Query: DD metric `sum:trace.aspnet_core.request.hits.by_http_status{service:ms-account-api,env:prod,http.status_class:4xx}.as_count()`, 1h window ending at fire time (2026-08-09T09:46:19Z–10:46:19Z)
  • Observed: 2 total hits (1 @10:15:00Z, 1 @10:30:00Z) — far under the 300/15min threshold
  • Corroboration: `service:ms-account-api status:error` in DD Logs, 2026-08-09T10:16:19Z–11:00:00Z → 0 hits
  • Reasoning: same monitor-sensitivity/config-artifact non-reproduction shape as 49 prior occurrences — monitor transitions state without a real 4xx breach

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299551518
  • DD logs: https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Ams-account-api%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1786270579000&to_ts=1786273200000&live=false
  • Kibana: n/a — this KB is DD-APM-sourced, not ES-sourced

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #116 (last_notified_at was 2026-08-08T11:33:00Z — ~27h31m ago, 24h suppression window had expired).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (runtime-core-subscriber component; the entry's mobile-notifications sibling maps to `Admin` — split by service)
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: monitor ID is one of the 5 sibling IDs, name matches '[CRM] <service> throughput dropped (possible stall)' or '[CRM] <service> heartbeat — consumer silent'. 2) Pull `scripts/dd_search.py metric --query 'sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:<name>,env:prod}.as_rate()'` over a multi-hour window — expect a genuine but brief dip below the monitor's floor, not a data gap/tool failure. 3) Confirm `service:<name> status:error` in DD Logs returns 0 for the window. 4) Check the sibling outbound-5xx / P95-latency monitor for the same service — if also OK throughout, this is very likely the benign quiet-period pattern, not a real stall. 5) If a fire is still unresolved after ~1h, or a sibling error/latency monitor co-fires, escalate. 6) Do not re-investigate from scratch on each recurrence — log occurrence count and compare shape against this entry.
Open Jira: n/a — fix_status monitoring-noise-suspected-unconfirmed

Source alerts (1 total):
  • n/a — degraded cycle, no Slack MCP this session (proxy: DD monitor 302057011, fired 2026-08-09T15:04:32Z)

Root-cause analysis:
  • Query: DD metric `avg(last_15m):sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:runtime-core-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate()`, window 2026-08-09T14:30:00Z–15:20:00Z
  • Observed: sustained sub-2-msg/s values immediately pre-fire (14:47:00Z–15:04:00Z mostly 0.05–2.2 msg/s, under the 2 msg/s 15m-avg threshold); one unrelated ~105 msg/s burst at 14:40:00–14:46:40Z had fully decayed before the fire
  • Corroboration: `service:runtime-core-subscriber status:error` in DD Logs, 2026-08-09T14:30:00Z–15:20:00Z → 0 hits
  • Reasoning: same absolute-floor-throughput-check-trips-on-quiet-period shape as 115 prior occurrences across the 5-sibling monitor family — no corroborating error signal, no confirmed real stall
